phil-epi-01-c2.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2001). The Analysis of Knowledge. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-01-c2.quote: According to this analysis, justified true belief is necessary and sufficient for knowledge.
phil-epi-01-c2.claim: Together these three JTB conditions seemed to many philosophers to be necessary and sufficient for knowledge.

phil-epi-01-c3.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2021). Knowledge How. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-01-c3.quote: knowledge-how and knowledge-that are distinct kinds of knowledge
phil-epi-01-c3.claim: Gilbert Ryle argued that it can't be fully reduced to propositions.

phil-epi-03-c1.text: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Gettier Problems. Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-03-c1.quote: He and Jones have applied for a particular job.
phil-epi-03-c1.claim: Classic case: Smith and Jones are competing for a job.

phil-epi-03-c1.text: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Gettier Problems. Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-03-c1.quote: But Smith has been told by the company president that Jones will win the job.
phil-epi-03-c1.claim: The boss tells Smith that Jones will get it.

phil-epi-04-c1.text: Steup, Matthias, Neta, Ram (2005). Epistemology. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-04-c1.quote: Therefore, justification is determined solely by those internal factors that you and your envatted brain doppelganger share.
phil-epi-04-c1.claim: Two broad camps disagree: Internalism: justification supervenes only on factors internal to the believer, what they are aware of or can access by reflection.

phil-epi-05-c3.text: Brogaard, Berit, Salerno, Joe (2002). Fitch’s Paradox of Knowability. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-epi-05-c3.quote: It is the proof that shows (in a normal modal logic augmented with the knowledge operator) that “all truths are knowable” entails “all truths are known”
phil-epi-05-c3.claim: The Knowability Paradox (Fitch): if all truths are knowable, then all truths are known, which is absurd for finite knowers.
